from: Brandon's review note of 2026-11-25, item 2, and his note 15 of the same day. The words of every line are his, unchanged, but for one: line n8.3, where he wrote "It was a body." and then asked the Builder to choose a stronger word ("being" or "titan", or the Builder's own). The positions, the marks, the replacement lines and the notes are the Builder's. In note 15 he liked everything else as it was shown to him, so in every marked line the replacement named by "stands" is the one that will be spoken; his own words stay in "text" beside it. This is a draft on the table: narration.clips in config/showcase.json still holds the approved script until he writes that the script is final.

lines.text: Past the last calm water, there is a shore.
Nothing on it has a name.
Nothing on it should be alive.
All of it is.

lands.what: the first strike of the music, where the strait opens

lines.text: The strait.
Blades of stone, taller than the storms that break on them.

mark.why: 6.4 s, and the strait has 4.3 s left after "The strait." and its pause. As written, its last 2 s are said over the colony, and it pushes the feeding line off the feeders.

replace.text: Stone blades, taller than the storms.
Stone blades. Storms break on them.

lines.text: At low tide the winged ones come down to feed. They do not have long.

mark.why: 7.8 s over two shots that last 7.1 s together, the colony and the feeders. Its last second is said over the drowned, the picture of the next line.

replace.text: At low tide the winged ones feed. They do not have long.
At low tide the winged ones come down to feed. Not for long.
replace.note: Keeps "come down", and leaves about half the room to spare that the first one leaves.

lines.text: High in the weed hangs one that stayed. Then the sea returns. All at once.
The fire.
A lake of it, under a black skin.
The tall ones walk the skin, and drink from the cracks.
Sometimes the skin gives way. The fire beneath has never cooled.

mark.why: Its two sentences fall on each other's pictures. The cut shows the fire under the skin first and the one that sank second; the line says the skin gives way first and the fire second. It is also tight: 7.2 s over two shots of 6.9 s.

replace.text: The fire has never cooled. Sometimes the skin gives way.
The fire beneath has never cooled. Sometimes the skin gives way.
replace.note: Your own words in the other order. Tight: it has to start in the last quarter second of the shot before.

lines.text: The pits.
lines.note: The shot is the shelf with one pit steaming on it. The line says pits.

lines.text: The ground breathes here. Slow. From far below.
Red growth crowds the rim, feeding on the breath.

mark.why: 5.3 s on a shot of 3.6 s. Whole, it fits only if it starts at 1:19.3, and then its first 1.8 s are said over the shaft, before the red growth is on screen.

replace.text: Red growth feeds on the breath.
Red growth crowds the rim.

lines.text: The pale herds graze the channel, and never the rim. One did.

mark.why: It fits for length. But the shot it ends on shows two animals at the rim: the dead one the line means, and behind it a living one with its head down, feeding at the rim, as the line says never the rim.

replace.text: The pale herds graze the channel, not the rim. One did. One will.
The pale herds keep to the channel. One did not. One will not.

lines.text: The red flats.
The ground still bleeds here. No rain made this.

mark.why: It fits for length, and it has to end before the pool bursts on the music's strike, so it cannot sit later. But 3.6 of its 5.5 s are said over the stalks, which it does not name. The red they stand in is in view; the stalks are what the shot is about. Each replacement names them and keeps one of your two sentences.

replace.text: Stalks root in the red. The ground still bleeds.
Stalks root in the red. No rain made this.

lines.text: The heavy ones wallow in it, and grow fat.
The salt keeps whatever it catches. Forever.
The ridge.
Above the cloud. Above the storm.

mark.why: It fits for length. "Above the cloud" matches: the cloud sea lies below. "Above the storm" does not: the shot is the ridge in the storm, with storm cloud around the spire and lightning on it, and the next line has the lightning walk the ridge.

replace.text: Above the cloud. Under the storm.
Above the cloud. Inside the storm.

lines.text: Every night the lightning walks it. Spire to spire.
lines.note: Its first sentence is said over the kites and then over the animal the lightning killed. Neither is named.

lines.text: The herds shelter in the hollow beneath, and wait for morning.

mark.why: 6.7 s in a shot of 7.2 s, the last of the place. On paper it fits with 0.3 s to spare, and the estimate has been wrong by more than that. If the read comes out long, its last word is said over the lake.

replace.text: The herds shelter in the hollow beneath, until morning.
The herds wait out the night in the hollow beneath.

lines.text: The lake.
Still. Gold at the edge. Black at the center.
lines.note: "Black at the center." is said over the edge, where the black water lies behind a skeleton on the lip. The centre itself comes two shots later.

lines.text: The herds drink at the shallows. None of them looks down.

mark.why: 6.5 s on a shot of 5.4 s. Its last second is said over the centre, and it pushes the last line of the place past the end of the place.

replace.text: The herds drink. None of them looks down.
The herds come to drink. None looks down.

lines.text: The center has no floor. Something there looks back.

mark.why: 6.0 s in a shot of 6.3 s, the last of the place, and only if the line before it is shortened. On paper it then fits with 0.2 s to spare. If the read comes out long, its last word is said over the first frames of the Reveal.

replace.text: The center has no floor. Something looks back.
No floor at the center. Something looks back.

lines.text: From high enough, the land has a shape.

mark.why: 4.3 s where 2.8 s are free. It cannot start before the camera has left the water, about 2:40.5, and the line after it has to be out before the strike at 2:47.1. Whole, it fits only from 2:39.0, on the water, where "from high enough" would be said at lake level.

replace.text: The land has a shape.
From above, a shape.

lines.text: None of it was ever land.

lands.what: the reveal strike of the music

lines.text: It was a titan.

lands.what: the reveal strike of the music

lines.note: Brandon wrote "It was a body." and on 2026-11-25 (note 15) asked for a stronger word, "being" or "titan" or the Builder's choice. "Titan" is chosen: it is the word the whole build uses for it, it says how large it is, and the line keeps its five syllables and its stress, so its timing does not move. Placed so the line starts on the strike, on the frame where the whole body is in view. The cut's own rule keeps speech clear of the four strikes; it is lifted for this one line when the script is final. If the word "titan" should fall on the strike instead, the line starts about 0.6 s earlier.

lines.text: Everything here feeds on it. And it is not finished.

lands.what: the beat where the Heart's glow pulses once on the body

lines.note: Placed where the approved script had its last line. It can sit up to 5 s later if the beat should answer "not finished".

unnamed.what: The vessel mouth and the lava fall: 7.2 s with no line, under the biggest peak of the music at 1:06.8. I would leave it without words.
The stalks. Line n5.2 is said over them and no line names them. Both replacements for n5.2 do.
The kites streaming from the spire. The end of n6.2 and the start of n6.3 are said over them.
The animal the lightning killed. "Every night the lightning walks it." is said over it, which fits in sense, and nothing names the animal.
The skeleton on the lip of the lake. "Black at the center." is said over it.

rules: Short, blunt lines, and not every line about dying: by my reading 5 of the 32 lines are about dying or the dead (n2.4, n3.4, n4.4, n5.4 and n8.4). The longest line is n2.4, at 8.8 s.
